doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Billy Taylor years and the greats
title: Day job, Birdland and generosity with money
summary: Billy Taylor's Birdland offer led May to leave an insurance day job; he earned more on weekends and tells how he tips freely.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: From a business and economic standpoint, was it a decent living for you in those years, in the 50s?

Oh yeah. I’ll tell you why, because not being trained at all, not playing the bass left handed like that, I couldn’t study formally or anything like that. So I just wound up saying to myself I’m going to have a day job during the week, I don’t know, five days a week or whatever, and I’ll work on the weekends just playing weddings and bar mitzvahs and things like that. And then actually Billy Taylor was the one that made the decision for me, because I’m thinking that I’m just married and I’ve got a young baby you know and I want to be a good provider you know. And Billy asked me to open Birdland with him and make all these gigs, and be a steady member of his trio, and I’m saying well I

don’t know, I don’t know. I don’t want to have to scuffle. And finally I just took a chance. My wife game me an opportunity. She said well you just follow your mind. I’m very happy I did that because on the weekends I would make three times the money I would make on my day job, working for an insurance company at that time and playing, like I said, playing with all these other people. So financially it was really very good. But my wife at that time told me that I was too giving. I’m always giving my money away and buying people drinks and—
Oh man, big sporty orty here. Really. Oh I’ve got a live one.

I’m still that way. I just made a record date with Jane [Jarvis] and Benny and Grady. [Tate]. And at the end of the date she treated us financially very well. So I put the check in my pocket and I told Benny I said, “Ah, Benny, I’ve got some money, I can start tipping again.” He fell on the floor. Because I do that a lot. I feel that that’s what it’s for, to share a little bit. People are working and giving you a service, you treat them nice. So I went right down to the garage and took my car, I gave that guy a six dollar tip.
Well now I know why everybody says nice things about you.
Yeah, I don’t know what it is.
